title: Comparing & Ordering Numbers
description: Learn to compare and order numbers up to 10,000 for Class 3 — using place value, the symbols >, < and =, and arranging numbers in ascending and descending order.

topics.title: Comparing Numbers
topics.concept:
To compare two numbers means to find which is bigger, which is smaller, or whether they are equal. We use three signs:

  • > means greater than (the open mouth eats the bigger number).
  • < means less than.
  • = means equal to.

The place-value rule: always start from the left (the biggest place). The number with more digits is bigger. If they have the same number of digits, compare the thousands first, then hundreds, then tens, then ones — stop as soon as one digit is bigger.

examples.solution: 1002 has 4 digits and 999 has only 3 digits. More digits means a bigger number, so 1002 > 999.

recap: Compare numbers starting from the LEFT (the biggest place value).
A number with more digits is greater.
> means greater than, < means less than, = means equal to.

topics.title: Ordering Numbers
topics.concept:
When we put many numbers in order we can arrange them two ways:

  • Ascending order — smallest to biggest (going up), like climbing stairs.
  • Descending order — biggest to smallest (going down).

To order numbers, compare them in pairs using place value, then line them up.

recap: Ascending order goes from smallest to biggest.
Descending order goes from biggest to smallest.
Compare with place value, then line the numbers up.

questions.explanation: 3210 has the largest hundreds/tens after the same thousands.
999 has 3 digits; 1000 has 4, so 999 is smaller.
4005 has the smallest hundreds/tens after the same thousands.

questions.q: When comparing 5631 and 5639, which place decides the answer?
questions.explanation: All match until the ones: 1 vs 9.

questions.q: Which list is in ascending order?
Make the GREATEST 4-digit number using 7, 0, 5, 3 (each once).
Make the SMALLEST 4-digit number using 7, 0, 5, 3 (no leading zero).
I am greater than 2500 and less than 2510. I am even and end in 4. Who am I?
Which sign makes it true:  3 thousands ___ 30 hundreds ?
questions.explanation: 3 thousands = 3000 and 30 hundreds = 3000, so they are equal.
